footer.tagline: A video sharing platform whose HLS transcoding runs automatically on a serverless container and event-driven architecture.
footer.authors: Dinh Quoc Cuong (523H0008) & Vo Huynh Minh Duc (523H0014) · Supervisor: MSc. Mai Van Manh

landing.heroSubtitle: Adaptive bitrate transcoding to three renditions (360p, 720p, 1080p), driven asynchronously by events on an AWS serverless container architecture (AWS Batch, Fargate Spot and CloudFront).
landing.statCostDesc: Fargate Spot scaling to zero, against an EC2 instance billed around the clock while idle.
landing.statCdnDesc: Smooth HLS playback through CloudFront with Origin Access Control.
landing.statAbrDesc: Resolution adapts automatically to the viewer's available bandwidth.
landing.statCicdDesc: Eleven Terraform modules and five GitHub Actions workflows with DevSecOps checks.
landing.featuresSubtitle: An end-to-end solution from upload, through asynchronous transcoding, to secure multi-rendition delivery on AWS.
landing.featureHlsDesc: An FFmpeg container splits the source into six-second `.ts` segments and writes a `master.m3u8` listing three renditions (360p, 720p, 1080p).
landing.featureScaleDesc: An AWS Batch job on Fargate Spot releases every resource when no video is waiting (scale to zero), which removes the cost of idle capacity.
landing.featureEventDesc: The asynchronous pipeline connects an Amazon S3 event notification, an Amazon SQS queue, an AWS Lambda submitter and MongoDB Atlas.
landing.featureCdnDesc: Origin Access Control keeps the processed bucket entirely private, blocking direct public access while delivering video quickly worldwide.
landing.featureThemeDesc: A modern viewing experience with a smooth light and dark theme switch, remembered in the browser.
landing.featureCicdDesc: Automated Jest unit tests, Gitleaks secret scanning, Trivy container scanning and k6 load testing.
landing.archSubtitle: Four automated steps from upload to playback, built on managed AWS components.
landing.archStep1: The browser uploads the video straight to Amazon S3 through a pre-signed URL, so no file passes through the backend.
landing.archStep2: S3 emits an event to an Amazon SQS queue, which triggers an AWS Lambda function to submit the transcoding job.
landing.archStep3: An FFmpeg container starts on Fargate Spot, produces the HLS renditions, and releases every resource when it finishes.
landing.archStep4: CloudFront delivers the HLS stream worldwide, protected by OAC, to the HLS.js player in the browser.
landing.codeTag: Lambda job submitter · real source code
landing.ctaSubtitle: Share videos online with automatic HLS transcoding and a modern interface.
